**RE: Urgent Member Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Patient Name:** Taylor Ellison
*   **Member ID:** W423241591
*   **Reference Number:** POC-C4BC2EBAC7-30163
*   **Requested Service:** Shoulder labral / instability repair
*   **Procedure Code:** CPT 29806
*   **Requesting Surgeon:** Dr. Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeal Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the prior authorization denial dated August 14, 2026, for my scheduled shoulder labral and instability repair (CPT 29806). The denial letter states that the "clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is incorrect. My clinical records document a highly compliant, extensive trial of conservative treatment that fully satisfies the criteria outlined in your governing medical policy, Carelon Medical Benefits Management’s "Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery" (Doc ID: MSK02-1125.1, Effective Date: November 15, 2025). 

Below, I map the clinical facts of my case to the exact criteria required by the policy to demonstrate complete medical necessity.

### 1. Documented Trial of Conservative Treatment (Addressing the Denial Reason)
The policy states that medical necessity requires a "Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management (unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management)*" and defines the requirements as follows:
> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My clinical records show that I completed the following conservative care regimen:
*   **Physical Therapy (PT) Program:** I completed **16 weeks** of active, supervised physical therapy from April 1, 2026, to July 22, 2026, totaling **18 completed visits**. This program was directed by a licensed physical therapist and focused specifically on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening. This exceeds the policy's 12-week minimum and is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This directly satisfies the policy's definition: "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: • Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services • Supervised home treatment program..."
*   **Complementary Conservative Strategies:** The policy requires at least one complementary strategy. I utilized multiple strategies, including:
    1.  **Anti-inflammatory Medications:** I utilized NSAIDs consistently for 4 months to manage symptomatic flares. This satisfies the policy's complementary option: "Prescription strength anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics"
    2.  **Activity Modification:** I practiced strict activity modification under medical guidance for several months. This satisfies the policy's complementary option: "Alternative therapies such as acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors) where applicable"
*   *Note on Injections:* Therapeutic injections were not pursued because they are clinically inappropriate and not indicated for recurrent glenohumeral instability.

Despite completing more than 4 months of comprehensive conservative management, my shoulder remains unstable, painful, and prone to dislocation, representing a clear conservative treatment failure.

### 2. Clinical Evidence of Instability and General Medical Necessity
My clinical presentation and imaging meet all of the specific diagnostic criteria required under the policy:
> "Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met:
> • History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation
> • Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift)
> • Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living
> • MRI demonstrates at least ONE of the following:
> o A labral lesion consistent with the clinical instability
> o Hill-Sachs lesion
> o Capsular tear
> o Capsular redundancy with clinical multidirectional instability"

My medical records map perfectly to each of these points:
*   **History of Dislocation/Subluxation:** I have suffered from 9 months of recurrent shoulder instability with apprehension. Since my symptoms began, I have experienced three distinct anterior dislocations, the most recent of which required manual reduction in the Emergency Department. 
*   **Instability Physical Exam Findings:** During my physical evaluation, Dr. Marchetti documented classic "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift)", including positive apprehension and relocation tests, as well as increased anterior translation on the load-and-shift test.
*   **Interference with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):** My shoulder instability severely interferes with my daily life and livelihood. I must actively avoid overhead reaching, and I am completely unable to return to my work duties, which require lifting.
*   **Advanced Imaging Verification:** An MR arthrogram of my shoulder performed on June 3, 2026, demonstrated an "anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion." This objectively satisfies the criteria requiring an MRI that demonstrates "A labral lesion consistent with the clinical instability" as well as a "Hill-Sachs lesion." My glenoid bone loss is minimal (under 10 percent), and my rotator cuff remains fully intact.

### Conclusion
I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29, no active infection, and no untreated substance use. I have no clinical contraindications to surgery. My records clearly document that I have failed a 16-week trial of conservative treatment and meet all requirements for surgical stabilization under your joint surgery policy guidelines. 

I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for CPT 29806 so that I may undergo this necessary repair, stabilize my shoulder, and return to work safely.

Please contact my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, at [Dr. Marchetti's Clinic Phone Number] or contact me directly if you require any further documentation.

Sincerely,

Taylor Ellison
[Taylor Ellison's Signature]
